items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I went around there, John Pantone, took the job, and went to come on with me and went to play it. He blowed the trombone.

ctx.x: Talked sort of Creole? Ed Waugh?

Well, he didn't, he didn't talk, he never talked in broken, you know, Creole, but he was from, you know, from that home out there, you see? His old daddy used to talk in broken English like that, you know? But not him, cause he practically came, he must have came here when he was young, you know? He was a good trumpet player. He had plenty, plenty of work out there in the country, everything given. Well, there's another trumpet player, Pendleton. That, uh, you talking about John Pendleton. Yeah, did he? Well, he…
But he could play trumpet. I never knew, if somebody told, mention the name of other, just, you knew what he was

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: The interviewer mentions John Pendleton in the context of Frank taking the band, but the interviewee (Eddie Dawson) does not mention John Pendleton, nor does he confirm any personal interaction or relationship with him.

ctx.x: And that Pelican band from uptown there, what you call them, playing trumpet there, Eddie, and they had a, what's the name, uh, it was Frankie Duesen. Frankie Duesen.

Oh, yeah. Well, that was the town, that was, uh, that was Ragtime band. Yeah. That was Ragtime band. They had the Frank's, ah, alright. I think that was a good one. That's when Frank takes the band, and he left John Pendleton, well, John Pendleton, you know, he could play a kind of style of music. No. Well, I had another fella. His name was Ned. Yeah. Yeah. That's Terry's band, but men like to travel around, so he went away. See, Frank's taken up on Edwark Clem.

Edwark Clem, well, that's the one I was talking about on the trumpet, Edwark Clem. Oh, yeah. He was another fella that had one eye, too. He used to wear black glasses all the time. You couldn't tell it. My glasses are such an app. Yeah. But he was a good trumpet player, though. Oh, yeah.
